items.chapter: Chapter 6.
items.exact_text: Quia non de verbis solum Scripturae, sed etiam de sensu plurima controversia est, si ecclesiae interpretatio non est certa intelligendi norma, ecquis erit istiusmodi controversiae judex? Sensum enim suum pro sua virili quisque defendet; quod si in exploranda verbi Dei intelligentia nullus est certus judex, audemus dicere nullam rempublicam fuisse stultius constitutam. Sin autem apostoli tradiderunt ecclesiis verbum Dei sine intelligentia verbi Dei, quomodo praedicarunt evangelium omni creaturae? quomodo docuerunt omnes gentes servare quaecunque illis fuerunt a Christo commendata Non est puerorum aut psittacorum praedicatio, qui sine mente dant, accipiuntque sonum,
items.translation_text: Modern Translation: Because the greatest controversy is not only about the words of Scripture but also about their meaning; if the church"s interpretation is not a certain standard for understanding, who then will be the judge of such a controversy? For everyone will defend his own interpretation as best he can; but if there is no certain judge for examining the understanding of the Word of God, we dare to say that no commonwealth was ever more foolishly constituted. But if the apostles handed down the Word of God to the churches without the understanding of the Word of God, how did they preach the gospel to every creature? How did they teach all nations to observe whatever was entrusted to them by Christ? The preaching of boys or parrots, who give and receive sound without mind, is not preaching. (Roman Catholic Apologist, Unknown, Unknown)

items.chapter: Chapter 8.
items.exact_text: una cum ejusdem disciplinae regimine consociavit. Sic appellatur ecclesia Gallicana, Anglicana Germanica particularis, ut distinguatur ab universali illa Christianorum societate; quae omnes Christiani nominis nationes complectitur. At uti supradiximus, eeclesiae nomen non proprie convenire societati omnium Christianorum, eo modo quo convenit particularibus Christianorum coetibus; sic consequens est, ut dicamus, eeclesiae nomen non competere in eam multarum ecclesiarum particularium consociationem eodem plane modo. Vocetur ergo certe ecclesiarum quae sunt in Gallia communio inter ipsas, et ecclesia, si ecclesia est multarum ecclesiarum confoederatio, non si nomen ecelesiae ex usu Scripturae sacrae accipiatur. Paulus enim varias ecclesias particulares quae erant in [[BLOCKQUOTE]] Achaia, ecclesias Achaliae nuncupat, non ecclesiam Achaiae vel ecclesiam Achaicam,
items.translation_text: Modern Translation: has associated together with the government of the same discipline. Thus a particular Gallican, Anglican, or German church is spoken of, to distinguish it from that universal society of Christians which embraces all nations of the Christian name. But as we have said above, the name of church does not properly belong to the society of all Christians in the same way it belongs to particular assemblies of Christians; thus it follows that we must say the name of church does not apply to that association of many particular churches in exactly the same way. Therefore, let the communion among themselves of the churches which are in Gaul certainly be called a church, if a church is a federation of many churches, but not if the name of church is taken from the usage of Sacred Scripture. For Paul calls the various particular churches which were in Achaia, the churches of Achaia, not the church of Achaia or the Achaian church. (Unknown Protestant Divine, Unknown Work, Unknown Location)

items.chapter: An Answer to a Late Treatise About the Nature of Schism.
items.exact_text: Sed praeterea quaenam ista est, quaeso, ordinaria vocatio, quam eos habuisse dicis, quos Deus paucis quibusdam exceptis, excitavit? Certe papistica. Nam haec tua verba sunt; hodie si episcopi Gallicanarum ecclesiarum se et suas ecclesias a tyrannide episcopi Romani vindicare velint, et eas ab omni idololatria et superstitione repurgare, non habent opus alia vocatione ab ea quam habent. Quid ergo? Papisticas ordinationes, — in quibus neque morum examen praecessit, neque leges ullae servatae sunt inviolabiliter ex divino jure in electionibus et ordinationibus [f53] praescriptae, in quibus puri etiam omnes canones impudentissime violati sunt: quae nihil aliud sunt, quam foedissima Romani prostibuli nundinatio, quavis meretricum mercede, quam Deus templo suo inferri prohibuit, inquinatior: quibus denique alii non ad praedicandum sed pervertendum evangelium: alii non ad docendum, sed ad rursus sacrificandum, et ad abominandum βδέλυγμα sunt ordinati, — usque adeo firmas tecum esse censebimus, ut quoties tali cuipiam pseudoepiscopo Deus concesserit, ad verum Christianismum transire, omnis ilia istiusmodi ordinationis impuritas simul expurgata censeatur? Imo quia sic animum per Dei gratiara mutavit, quo ore, quo pudore, qua conscientia papismum quidem detestabitur, suam autem inordinatissimam ordinationem non ejurabit? aut si, ejuret, quomodo ex illius jure auctoritatem dicendi habebit? Nec tamen nego quin tales, si probe doctrinam veram tenere, si honestis moribus praediti, si ad gregem pascendum apti comperiantur, ex pseudoepiscopis novi pastores, legitime designentur.
items.translation_text: Modern Translation: But furthermore, what, I ask, is that ordinary calling, which you say those men had, whom God raised up, with a few exceptions? Certainly it is Papistical. For these are your words: 'today if the bishops of the Gallican churches wish to vindicate themselves and their churches from the tyranny of the Roman bishop, and purge them from all idolatry and superstition, they have no need of another calling than the one they have.' What then? Papistical ordinations, — in which no examination of morals preceded, nor were any laws kept inviolable which were prescribed by divine right in elections and ordinations, in which even all the pure canons were most impudently violated: which are nothing else than the most foul trafficking of the Roman brothel, more defiled than any prostitute's wage, which God forbade to be brought into his temple: by which, finally, some are ordained not to preach but to pervert the gospel: others not to teach, but to sacrifice again, and to an abominable abomination — shall we judge these to be so firm with you, that as often as God grants to such a pseudo-bishop to pass over to true Christianity, all the impurity of such an ordination is deemed purged at the same time? Rather, because he has so changed his mind by the grace of God, with what face, with what shame, with what conscience will he indeed detest Papism, but will not abjure his most irregular ordination? Or if he abjures it, how will he have the authority to speak from its right? Nor yet do I deny that such men, if they are found to hold true doctrine uprightly, if they are endowed with honest morals, if they are apt to feed the flock, may be legitimately designated as new pastors from pseudo-bishops. (Theodore Beza, De Diversis Gradibus Ministrorum, N/A)

items.chapter: A Brief Vindication of the Nonconformists From the Charge of Sc
items.exact_text: Coitio Christianorum merito sane illicita, si illicitis par; merito damnanda, si quis de ea queritur eo titulo quo de factionibus querela est. In cujus perniciem aliquando convenimus? Hoc sumus congregati quod et dispersi; hoc universi quod et singuli; neminem laedentes, neminem contristantes; quum probi, cum boni coeunt, cum pii, cum casti congregantur, non est factio dicenda, sed curia.
items.translation_text: Modern Translation: This gathering of Christians is indeed rightfully illicit, if it is on a par with illicit groups; it is rightfully to be condemned, if anyone complains of it under the same title as one complains of factions. For whose destruction do we ever assemble? Gathered together, we are the same as when dispersed; all together we are what we are individually, injuring no one, grieving no one. When the upright, when the good assemble, when the pious, when the chaste gather, it is not to be called a faction, but a court. (Tertullian, Apologeticum, 39)

items.chapter: A Survey of the Fifth Chapter.
items.exact_text: Ne admittam culpam, ego meo sum promus pectori, Suspicio est in pectore alieno sita. Nam nunc ego te si surripuisse suspicer, Jovi coronam de capite e Capitolio, Quod in culmine astat summo, si non id feceris, Atque id tamen mihi lubeat suspicarier; Qui tu id prohibere me potes, ne suspicer,
items.translation_text: Modern Translation: I am the steward of my own breast to ensure I do not commit a fault; suspicion resides in another's breast. items.exact_text: "Si quis, aut privatus aut publicus, eorum decreto non stetit, sacrificiis interdicunt. Haec poena apud eos est gravissima. Quibus ira est interdictum, ii numero impiorum et sceleratorum habentur: iis omnes decedunt, aditum eorum sermonemque defugiunt, ne quid ex contagione incommodi accipiant; neque iis petentibus jus redditur, neque honos ullus communicatur. His autem omnibus Druidibus prsaeest unus, qui summam inter eos habet authoritatem. Hoc mortuo, si quis ex reliquis excellit dignitate, succedit: at si sunt plures pares, suffragio Druidum 753 allegitur, nonnunquam etiam armis de principetu contendunt." — Caes. lib. 6:13, de Bell. Gall.
items.modern_reference: Modern Citation: Julius Caesar, Commentarii de Bello Gallico (Commentaries on the Gallic War), Book 6, Chapter 13.
items.translation_text:
Modern Citation: Julius Caesar, Commentarii de Bello Gallico (Commentaries on the Gallic War), Book 6, Chapter 13.
Translation: “If any private or public person has not stood by their decree, they forbid him from sacrifices. This punishment among them is most severe. Those who are so interdicted are counted among the impious and criminal; all withdraw from them, avoid their approach and conversation, lest they receive any harm from contact with them; nor is justice rendered to them when they seek it, nor is any honor shared with them. Over all these Druids one presides, who has supreme authority among them. When he dies, if one of the rest is pre-eminent in dignity, he succeeds; but if several are equal, the matter is decided by the vote of the Druids, and sometimes they even contend for leadership by arms.”
